doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Musicians union today; teaching sight reading and standards at NYU
summary: She criticizes young musicians' lack of reading and standards and describes her NYU classes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What’s the state of the musicians union now? Are you aware of it?
Well I mean the thing is that so much has been done in synthesizers and those — I don’t know if anybody writes anything real anymore. I mean have you listened?

Oh it was the best. Because there was work for singers, it was really — one, if you could read — you had to read — and that’s why when I was teaching at NYU and I started a class ‘cause these kids are paying 60 grand a year, probably 80 now, and they’re not learning to read music and they’re music majors. Come on. And so I started a class for sight reading for singers, and another one for repertoire, ‘cause another one of the problems was they didn’t know, you know, standards. And I opened that to musicians as

well. Well they didn’t come. And a lot of the musicians, the young musicians, don’t know any standards. They go back to, you know — I think they’re finding out that they have to now, but there was a long period —
Uh huh. They’re not going to get called for a club date and play their own music.
Hey come on down and bring your original tunes.
Everybody can’t wait to hear them.
